analysis.investment_thesis: CAMS is a fantastic business — dominant mutual fund RTA infrastructure with 39% operating margins and ROE of 44% — but at P/E 40 and P/S 12.6, the market has already priced in a lot of India's mutual fund growth story, putting the PEG ratio above 2.0, well past my comfort zone.
key_strengths: Near-monopoly economics: 39.4% operating margins and ROE of 43.9% reflect durable pricing power as the dominant MF registrar/transfer agent in India
Asset-light model with virtually no debt (D/E 0.06) and consistent free cash flow: 359 Cr in FY25, growing from 184 Cr in FY20
Net profit CAGR of 18% over 7 years with consistently expanding revenue — genuine quality compounder with India's financialization as a tailwind
key_risks: PEG ratio of ~2.2 (P/E 40.1 / 18% growth) significantly exceeds my 1.5 threshold — valuation leaves no margin of safety
Zero promoter holding (0%) means no alignment anchor; business is entirely dependent on maintaining contracts with mutual fund houses that could consolidate
Revenue growth moderation risk: AUM-linked fee revenue depends on markets staying buoyant — a prolonged equity bear market could cut revenue sharply
red_flags: P/B of 15.25 and P/S of 12.6 reflect extremely premium valuation for a 11.6% revenue CAGR business — even great businesses can be bad investments at any price
Revenue growth has been lumpy: 706 Cr (2021) to 910 Cr (2022) was a step-change, but the 2021-2022 period benefited from the post-COVID AUM surge which may not repeat at the same pace
analysis.detailed_analysis:
CAMS is the kind of business I love finding — essential infrastructure in a growing ecosystem, high margins, low capital needs. Think of it as the 'picks and shovels' play on India's mutual fund revolution, where every new SIP account and every AUM rupee flowing into equity funds generates fee income for CAMS. With over 35 crore investor folios and a duopoly structure with KFintech, this has genuine moat characteristics.

But the price tag is the problem. At 40x earnings for a business compounding net profits at 18%, I'm paying 2.2x PEG — I want to pay under 1.0. The business could deserve re-examination closer to P/E 25-28 if earnings continue to compound at this rate. For now, if you own it, hold it; but I wouldn't be a buyer at these levels when better-valued GARP opportunities exist elsewhere in India.
